correctness.rationale: Finite equal-marginal joint distributions decompose as convex sums of normalized directed cycles. Parseval on the product cycles gives exactly the stated sine quotient for real test functions by conjugate pairing. Every nonzero coordinate contributes at least sin^2(pi/K). For two coordinates, sin^2(a+b)=sin^2 a+sin^2 b+2 sin a sin b cos(a+b) gives 2cos^2(pi/K) for K>=4; t>=3 is bounded by 1/(3sin^2(pi/K)), yielding exact B_2 through B_6. For K>=4, principal angular lengths delta>=pi/K obey sin^2(delta)>=q(pi/K)delta, since q(x)=sin^2(x)/x has a unique maximum and q(pi/4)=q(pi/2); this proves the high-support upper envelope. Uniform directed K-cycles with floor(tau K/pi) active unit frequencies attain the matching coefficient. The symbolic trigonometric identities and bounds are analytic; replayed finite scans and cosine-expectation checks are supplementary, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: B_K is the natural optimal dimension-free concentration factor already defined by the lead paper; its K/2 bound leaves a factor >2 gap in the sharp large-support slope. Determining B_K/K exactly and locating the first failure of the classical factor at support five resolves structurally motivated, previously unevaluated parts of that invariant. The argument applies over arbitrary coordinate counts, and the four-point robustness covers genuinely nonexchangeable directed cycles. These are not arbitrary finite slices or mere refactoring of the known sine quotient.
